battle.name: 斯洛伐克匈牙利戰爭
battle.theater: 斯洛伐克東部沙伊邊境戰場
battle.brief: 斯洛伐克匈牙利戰爭發生於1939年3月，匈牙利先占領喀爾巴阡魯塞尼亞，隨後向斯洛伐克東部邊境推進，戰事集中在沙伊及多瑙河上游附近。別丹步槍（Berdan rifle）是蘇聯陸軍當時仍在役的制式栓動步槍，但並非交戰雙方的主要武器。

kit.name: 別丹步槍
kit.history: 別丹步槍是蘇聯陸軍制式栓動步槍，長期作為步兵班排的基礎槍械，供步兵射手執行近距離作戰與一般邊防任務，至1939年仍列於現役。

countries: 交戰國是1939年3月14日宣布自治、16日起以獨立國家身分運作的斯洛伐克共和國，以及匈牙利王國。戰場集中在斯洛伐克東部與匈牙利接壤的山區，重要地點包括塔伊蒂、維什尼科馬爾尼克、拉博雷茨河谷，以及斯塔克欽、斯維德尼克、梅茲布羅德和斯尼納一帶。斯洛伐克把第一、第二山地旅，若干步兵部隊及邊防哨位調往東部；匈牙利則由西部軍團集群投入邊防營、步兵營、旅屬炮兵與偵察航空隊。這是一場未經正式宣戰、但正規軍彼此射擊並由最高軍事當局命令停火 的邊境戰爭，通常稱為斯洛伐克小戰爭、匈牙利小戰爭或馬萊戰爭。從1939年3月23日首次交火到4月4日簽署停火，延續約十二天，地理範圍大致沿斯洛伐克東側山脊和通往斯尼納的交通走廊展開。
countriesEn: The belligerents were the Slovak Republic, which declared autonomy on 14 March and began operating as an independent state on 16 March, and the Kingdom of Hungary. The fighting was concentrated in the mountainous eastern border region of Slovakia, particularly around Tajti, Vyšný Komárnik, the Laborec Valley, Stakčín, Svidník, Medzibrod, and Snina. Slovakia moved its 1st and 2nd Mountain Brigades, several infantry formations, and border outposts toward the east. Hungary committed formations from its western army-corps group, including border-guard battalions, infantry battalions, brigade artillery, and a reconnaissance aviation element. It was a border conflict that was never formally declared as a war, although regular troops exchanged fire and the highest military authorities ordered a ceasefire. It is commonly called the Little War, the Malá vojna in Slovak, or the Apró háború in Hungarian. From the first exchanges of fire on 23 March 1939 to the ceasefire signed on 4 April, the conflict lasted about twelve days along the eastern ridges of Slovakia and the transport approaches to Snina.
people: 斯洛伐克方面，總理兼政府首長約瑟夫·蒂索主持政治決定，陸軍總司令魯道夫·維斯特負責總動員、兵源調配及東線作戰指揮；卡羅爾·克拉帕萊克與揚·安布魯什等將領在山地旅指揮系統中部署兵力、接應邊防哨情報，並組織沿公路與山脊展開的局部反擊。匈牙利方面，總攝米克洛什·霍爾蒂是國家元首及最高軍事權威，總理帕爾·泰萊基負責內政與外交，參謀總長卡洛伊·貝雷格菲把軍團集群的部署轉化為前線命令，並協調邊防營接替正規步兵、調整炮兵與後勤。實際接觸初期多由營、連級指揮官依地形和道路狀況決定應變，因此前線情報速度、命令能否及時下達，以及山地道路上的補給是否跟上，常比名單上的總兵力更直接影響各次交火。停火談判則回到布拉迪斯拉發，由兩國軍事代表在德國與義大利的外交壓力下確認邊界及撤軍安排。
peopleEn: On the Slovak side, Prime Minister and government leader Jozef Tiso headed the political decisions, while commander of the Slovak Army Rudolf Viest directed the general mobilization, troop allocation, and operations on the eastern front. Generals such as Karol Klapálek and Ján Ambruš served within the mountain-brigade command system, deploying troops, responding to reports from the border outposts, and organizing local counterattacks along the roads and ridges. For Hungary, Regent Miklós Horthy was the head of state and supreme military authority. Prime Minister Pál Teleki handled domestic and diplomatic affairs, while Chief of the General Staff Károly Beregfy translated the dispositions of the western army-corps group into field orders and coordinated the replacement of border troops by regular infantry and the adjustment of artillery and logistics. During the initial contacts, battalion and company commanders often had to decide their responses from local terrain, road conditions, and the speed with which orders and reports arrived. Consequently, intelligence transmission, the speed of command, and the ability to supply troops along mountain roads affected individual engagements more directly than the nominal size of the mobilized forces. The ceasefire talks returned to Bratislava, where military representatives from both states confirmed the frontier and withdrawal arrangements under German and Italian diplomatic pressure.
kits: 雙方在1939年3月能夠使用的裝備差距並不像動員數字那樣懸殊，但供應與道路適應性不同。斯洛伐克步兵以vz. 30步槍、vz. 35步槍及vz. 27手槍為主，七點九毫米vz. 07輕機槍與vz. 24重機槍供班排及機槍組使用；炮兵包括七點五公分Škoda野戰砲、十五公分級榴彈砲及vz. 37三十七公分野戰砲。斯洛伐克亦接收了捷克斯洛伐克留下的LT vz. 35、LT vz. 38輕坦克，以及Avia B-135、B-534等航空器。匈牙利步兵主要使用三一M K毛瑟式步槍，並保有較舊的三五M步槍，手槍以九毫米Vis a Vis 32為代表，機槍口徑仍以七點九毫米為主，炮兵同樣使用七點五公分野戰砲與十五公分榴彈砲，並已有Fiat CR.32戰鬥機。vz. 30與匈牙利三一M K使用七點九乘五十四公釐長彈，vz. 35則使用較短的七點九乘三十九公釐彈；機槍彈、炮彈和步槍彈須分開儲運。斯洛伐克可用Tatra 111、Škoda 706等卡車配合鐵路與馬車，匈牙利也把汽車、馬匹和鐵路交接處並用。現有史料並不支持把上述每一型都投入前線，尤其坦克與飛機沒有在這場戰爭中形成決定性交鋒。
kitsEn: The equipment available to both sides in March 1939 was not as uneven as the mobilization figures might suggest, although logistics and suitability for mountain roads differed. Slovak infantry relied chiefly on the vz. 30 and vz. 35 rifles and the vz. 27 pistol, with the 7.92 mm vz. 07 light machine gun and vz. 24 heavy machine gun supporting platoons and machine-gun sections. Slovak artillery included the 7.5 cm Škoda field gun, 15-centimeter howitzers, and the vz. 37 37 mm anti-tank gun. Slovakia also inherited the Czechoslovak LT vz. 35 and LT vz. 38 light tanks and aircraft such as the Avia B-135 and B-534. Hungarian infantry primarily used the 31M K Mannlicher-type rifle and retained older 35M rifles, while the 9 mm Vis a Vis 32 was a representative service pistol. Machine guns remained predominantly chambered in 7.92 mm, and Hungarian artillery included 7.5 cm field guns and 15-centimeter howitzers. Fiat CR.32 fighters were already available to the Hungarian air force. The vz. 30 and Hungarian 31M K used the longer 7.92 × 54 mm R cartridge, whereas the vz. 35 used the shorter 7.92 × 39 mm round; machine-gun ammunition, artillery shells, and rifle ammunition therefore had to be stored and transported separately. Slovakia could combine Tatra 111 and Škoda 706 trucks with railways and horse-drawn transport, while Hungary likewise linked motor vehicles, horse teams, and railway transfer points. Surviving records do not show that every listed weapon or vehicle reached the front. In particular, tanks and aircraft did not engage in any decisive armored or air battle during the conflict.
tactics: 匈牙利方面利用斯洛伐克東部多條山間道路和河谷縱深推進，步兵通常沿公路成戰術縱隊前進，先以炮兵短暫壓制道路交叉處、溪流渡口和橋頭，再由工兵清除障礙，試圖奪取維什尼科馬爾尼克、斯塔克欽及斯尼納方向的控制點；後續部隊仍須沿有限道路展開，因此越過前線並不等於能迅速擴大戰果。斯洛伐克先以邊防哨提供早期警報，再由山地旅占領路旁高地和山脊，以交叉射擊、封閉道路及阻斷渡口遲滯越過邊界的縱隊；維什尼科馬爾尼克周邊的局部反擊迫使匈牙利攻勢放慢，卻未形成可以全面逆轉戰線的總反攻。斯方把部隊與彈藥由火車運到東線鐵路端點，再以卡車、馬車和人力向山地分散，匈牙利則由喀爾巴阡魯塞尼亞境內的基地供應前線。空軍主要執行偵察，也有有限的戰鬥及支援任務，但損失主要來自步兵射擊、機槍和炮兵交火。道路瓶頸、分散補給與缺乏大縱深，使全戰始終維持在邊境戰的規模，而未發展成坦克主導的會戰。
tacticsEn: Hungary advanced through several mountain roads and river valleys in eastern Slovakia. Infantry generally moved in tactical columns along the roads, using brief artillery fire to suppress road junctions, stream crossings, and bridgeheads before engineers attempted to clear obstacles and seize control of places such as Vyšný Komárnik, Stakčín, and the approaches to Snina. Because later formations still had to deploy along a limited number of roads, crossing the initial frontier did not automatically allow Hungary to expand its gains quickly. Slovakia relied first on border outposts to provide early warning, after which the mountain brigades occupied high ground and ridges beside the roads. Crossfire, blocked roads, and controlled crossings were used to delay Hungarian columns that had crossed the border. Local counterattacks around Vyšný Komárnik slowed the Hungarian advance, although they never developed into a general counteroffensive capable of reversing the entire front. Slovakia moved troops and ammunition by train to railheads in the east and then dispersed them by truck, horse-drawn transport, and carrying parties. Hungary supplied its forward forces from bases within Carpathian Ruthenia. Aviation was used mainly for reconnaissance and also for limited combat and support missions, but most losses resulted from infantry fire, machine guns, and artillery rather than large air attacks. Road bottlenecks, dispersed supply, and the lack of depth kept the entire conflict at the scale of a border war rather than allowing it to become a tank-led battle of maneuver.
data: 戰前經過是3月14日斯洛伐克宣布自治，3月15日至16日匈牙利完成對喀爾巴阡魯塞尼亞的占領，兩國邊界上的外交交涉隨即惡化。3月23日上午，匈牙利部隊在多處越過邊界，首批交火地點包括塔伊蒂；斯洛伐克邊防哨一面抵抗，一面把匈牙利推進方向送往縱深。首日交火後，布拉迪斯拉發政府下令總動員，第一、第二山地旅及其他步兵單位由鐵路和公路向東線集中。3月24日至27日，戰線沿塔伊蒂、維什尼科馬爾尼克及拉博雷茨河谷擴大，匈牙利縱隊向斯塔克欽、斯維德尼克和梅茲布羅德方向深入，斯洛伐克部隊則在道路交叉處及山脊據點進行局部反擊；到3月27日前後，匈牙利已在斯塔克欽與斯維德尼克方向取得縱深，但斯方仍守住維什尼科馬爾尼克一帶，使匈牙利軍不能沿鐵路迅速下切至斯尼納市區。3月28日至30日，匈牙利壓力伸展到斯尼納南側的接近地，斯洛伐克援軍及地方守軍鞏固現有陣地，雙方都未能包圍或摧毀對方主力。3月31日至4月3日，外交斡旋成為重點，前線仍有零星搜索與接觸，但沒有新的大規模突破。4月4日，兩國軍政代表在布拉迪斯拉發簽署停火協議，雙方隨後按停火線撤回及鞏固陣地。戰爭因此在約十二天內結束，斯洛伐克沒有失去中央政府與主要城市，匈牙利則保留前線占領區。
dataEn: The period immediately before the war was shaped by events from 14 March, when Slovakia declared autonomy, through 15 and 16 March, when Hungary completed its occupation of Carpathian Ruthenia. Diplomatic negotiations along the new frontier then deteriorated. On the morning of 23 March, Hungarian troops crossed the border at several points, and the first exchanges of fire included fighting at Tajti. The Slovak border outposts resisted while reporting the directions of the Hungarian advance. After the fighting on the first day, the Bratislava government ordered a general mobilization. The 1st and 2nd Mountain Brigades and other infantry units concentrated toward the eastern front by rail and road. From 24 to 27 March, the front extended through Tajti, Vyšný Komárnik, and the Laborec Valley. Hungarian columns pushed toward Stakčín, Svidník, and Medzibrod, while Slovak units mounted local counterattacks at road junctions and ridge positions. By about 27 March, Hungary had gained depth in the direction of Stakčín and Svidník, but the Slovaks still held the Vyšný Komárnik area and prevented the Hungarian force from moving rapidly down the railway toward the town of Snina. Between 28 and 30 March, Hungarian pressure reached the southern approaches to Snina. Slovak reinforcements and local troops consolidated their positions, and neither side was able to encircle or destroy the other’s main body. From 31 March to 3 April, diplomatic mediation became the principal development. Local patrols and contacts continued, but there was no new large-scale breakthrough. On 4 April, military and political representatives of both countries signed a ceasefire agreement in Bratislava, after which the troops withdrew to and consolidated the ceasefire line. The war therefore ended after about twelve days. Slovakia retained its central government and principal cities, while Hungary kept the territory it had occupied along the front.
cause: 直接背景是1938年11月的維也納第一次裁決。該裁決把喀爾巴阡魯塞尼亞及斯洛伐克南部大片土地割給匈牙利，留下斯洛伐克東部一段突出而彎曲的邊界；匈牙利在1939年3月占領喀爾巴阡魯塞尼亞後，又取得可向斯洛伐克山區展開的後方基地。匈牙利要求修正這段邊界，並取得通往斯尼納及更西側鐵路走廊的控制權，理由包括交通、戰略縱深與既有邊界不一致。斯洛伐克剛以獨立國家身分建立政權，沒有接受大幅割讓其剛繼承的領土。戰前數日的談判未能達成協議，匈牙利遂以越境占領作為既成事實，斯洛伐克則以總動員和山區阻擊維護原有國界。這場衝突因此不是兩國突然爆發的全面戰爭，而是第一次維也納裁決、匈牙利邊界修正計畫及斯洛伐克建國初期安全選擇交疊造成的有限軍事危機。
causeEn: The immediate background was the First Vienna Award of November 1938. It transferred Carpathian Ruthenia and a large area of southern Slovakia to Hungary, leaving a projecting and irregular frontier in eastern Slovakia. After Hungary occupied Carpathian Ruthenia in March 1939, it also obtained a rear base from which it could deploy into the Slovak mountains. Budapest sought to revise that frontier and gain control of the approaches to Snina and the railway corridor farther west, citing strategic depth, communications, and the inconsistency of the existing boundary. Slovakia had just begun operating as an independent state and did not accept a substantial cession of territory it had only recently inherited. Negotiations in the days before the fighting failed to produce an agreement. Hungary then attempted to create a fait accompli by crossing the frontier, while Slovakia answered with general mobilization and a mountain defense of its existing borders. The conflict was therefore not an unexpected general war between two states, but a limited military crisis created by the interaction of the First Vienna Award, Hungary’s border-revision policy, and the security choices made by Slovakia as it began building an independent state.
impact: 停火後，匈牙利實際控制並取得近兩千平方公里土地，範圍包括斯塔克欽與斯維德尼克兩區的大部，以及梅茲布羅德、斯尼納區的相關地段；邊界向北移動，使匈牙利能更直接銜接喀爾巴阡魯塞尼亞與斯尼納方向，斯尼納市區則仍由斯洛伐克保有。軍事上，斯洛伐克證明山地旅能利用狹窄道路和防禦地形延遲縱隊，維什尼科馬爾尼克周邊的局部反擊尤其阻止匈牙利迅速打通整條走廊；但總動員後的兵力指揮、鐵路卸載、彈藥分送及預備隊接續仍不足以扭轉所有已形成的越境突破。匈牙利則把邊界要求由外交要求轉變為可持續控制的地面成果。不同戰後彙整大致把斯洛伐克損失列為三十餘人陣亡、一百至二百餘人受傷，匈牙利為個位數至十餘人陣亡、二十餘人受傷；輕傷、未回報及俘虜認定方式不同，因此不宜把任何單一數字當作最終核定傷亡。外交上，德國與義大利都推動迅速收束，避免戰事牽動德國在波蘭方向的準備，而斯洛伐克政府及軍隊則在失去東部土地後仍得以繼續運作。
impactEn: After the ceasefire, Hungary gained control of and annexed close to two thousand square kilometres of Slovak territory. This included most of the districts of Stakčín and Svidník, together with portions of Medzibrod and Snina. The frontier moved northward, linking Hungary more directly with Carpathian Ruthenia and the approaches to Snina, while the town of Snina itself remained in Slovak hands. Militarily, Slovakia demonstrated that its mountain brigades could use narrow roads and defensive terrain to delay advancing columns. Local counterattacks around Vyšný Komárnik were particularly important in preventing Hungary from opening the entire corridor quickly. At the same time, command of the mobilized force, unloading from trains, distribution of ammunition, and the follow-up of reserves were not sufficient to reverse every penetration that had already occurred. Hungary converted a territorial demand from a diplomatic claim into physically controlled ground. Different postwar compilations generally place Slovak losses at several dozen dead and between one and slightly more than two hundred wounded, while Hungarian losses are usually given as somewhere from single digits to a little over ten dead and a few dozen wounded. Because accounts differed in the treatment of slight wounds, unreported personnel, and prisoners, no single exact total should be treated as a final audited figure. Diplomatically, Germany and Italy both favored a rapid settlement so that the conflict would not disrupt German preparations in the Polish direction, while the Slovak government and army remained operational despite the loss of territory in the east.
result: 4月4日在布拉迪斯拉發簽訂的停火協議確定了最終結果：斯洛伐克軍隊從匈牙利占領區撤回停火線，匈牙利則保留已取得的斯塔克欽、斯維德尼克、梅茲布羅德及斯尼納南部地段，並在之後將其納入匈牙利行政與防衛體系。停火不是一份全面和平條約，而是一項迅速終止戰鬥、劃定軍隊位置並暫時接受新邊界的安排；後續勘界和行政接管使停火線逐漸固定。斯洛伐克保住布拉迪斯拉發、科希策、斯尼納市區及國家主要軍事組織，匈牙利則沒有被追回任何實地控制。從戰術看，斯洛伐克在維什尼科馬爾尼克等地的抵抗成功延遲並限制匈牙利推進；從戰略結果看，匈牙利以有限戰鬥取得實質邊界收益，因此這是一場有限而明確的匈牙利戰略勝利，同時也是斯洛伐克成功拖延而未能逆轉的邊境戰爭。
resultEn: The ceasefire agreement signed in Bratislava on 4 April established the immediate result. Slovak troops withdrew from the occupied areas to the ceasefire line, while Hungary retained Stakčín, Svidník, Medzibrod, and the southern portion of the Snina district, subsequently incorporating those areas into Hungary’s administrative and defensive system. The ceasefire was not a comprehensive peace treaty. It was an arrangement intended to stop the fighting, fix troop positions, and provisionally accept the new frontier, after which demarcation and administrative takeover gradually made the line permanent. Slovakia retained Bratislava, Košice, the town of Snina, and the principal institutions of its armed forces, and Hungary was not forced to surrender any of the ground it actually controlled. Tactically, Slovak resistance around Vyšný Komárnik and other positions successfully delayed and restricted the Hungarian advance. Strategically, Hungary converted limited fighting into concrete territorial gains. The result was therefore a limited but unmistakable Hungarian strategic victory, accompanied by Slovak delaying successes that did not become a strategic reversal.
